feedback.problem:
If $g(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=10$ and $g(10)=5,$ then

${lim}_{x\to {10}^{+}}\frac{g(x)-\operatorname{log}⁡x}{3g(10)}=$
 {{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $g(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=10,$ we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to {10}^{+}}g(x)=g(10)=5.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {10}^{+}}\frac{g(x)-\operatorname{log}⁡x}{3g(10)} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to {10}^{+}}g(x)-{lim}_{x\to {10}^{+}}\operatorname{log}⁡x}{3g(10)} \\  & =\frac{5-\operatorname{log}⁡10}{3(5)} \\  & =\frac{5-1}{3(5)} \\  & =\frac{4}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
